description.narrative:
Vulnerable civilians who have been struggling with the compounded impacts of drought and inflation got caught in crossfire. According to initial reports, close to 100,000 people got displaced as a result of the conflict in Lasanod. As per our rapid assessment, over 30 villages across Sool region started hosting the displaced with some villages having outnumbering IDP households. The IDPs livein makeshift shelters in areas where basic services were already scarce. Access to food and safe water are the priority according to the reports and our rapid assessment team also noticed these needs.
We are proposing to target 7 locations (Taleex, Kalabaydh, Saaxdheer, Boocame, Yagoori, Guumays and Ceegaag) in Sool region. Based on our assessment collectively these locations are hosting 3,580 displaced households (approx. 21,480 people).
Garowe is capital of Puntland and hosting large, displaced population. Being administrative capital, there are many international and national NGOs and UN agencies are present and established in Garowe. In addition, Puntland administration, private sector and host communities can also extend humanitarian assistance. Diaspora community is also reported to extending assistance in Garowe and other areas. While we decided to focus on the proposed seven locations as they are difficult for Puntland or Somaliland administration to provide assistance – and presence of eighter of these administrations have alsopotential to further increase tension. It has been observed that displaced population who have reached to Garowe have more capacities e.g., host families, travel related expenses, affordability to rent a shelter in Garowe etc. compared to displaced families who were not able to travel that far and have taken refuge in propose seven locations by us. Thus, possibly it is comparatively easy to respond to Garowe and more aid options may be available to affected populations.

participating-org.narrative: In 2004 Oxfam Novib set up a Liaison Office in Nairobi, Kenya in order to support the Strengthening Somali Civil Society Program, at the request of the EU. This request was based on Oxfam Novib's work in Somalia to date, but intended to be more widely directed atthe entire civil society sector and the specific context in which it is operating in a post-conflict country. The program started with consulting local organisations in Somalia and Somaliland to get a complete picture of the sectors and regions where they are active, the challenges they face and the relationship between civil society, local political structures and the private sector. A program was then developed to strengthen the institutional development of Oxfam Novib's partners and those of other Oxfams, as well as a range of new NGOs. In the first year local consultants were trained in Somalia. They were then seconded to civil society organisations to build their capacity in financial and organisational management. Furthermore, workshops were organised on specific themes suchas human rights and the role of civil society in the Somali context. The Liaison Office is now going to support the expansion of the program, focussing on strengthening both organisation and project management, while facilitating more training in the fields of civic education, governance, human rights and women's rights, HIV and AIDS and child protection. Over the years, the Somalia Country Office has expanded its intervention on short term humanitarian response as well as development development interventions. In 2015/2016, a decision was reached to move the Country Programme operation, which was largely in Nairobi, from Nairobi to Hargeisa. The country office has a small office in Nairobi , Kenya and large operations office in Hargeisa, Somaliland.
